idiom_name: Express Router mounted per version + checked-in OpenAPI document enforced by a validator
implementation_notes: A Router mounted under a version prefix (app.use('/v1', v1Router)) is the whole host service: the routes are the published protocol and a schema validator (ajv against the OpenAPI/JSON-Schema document) is what makes the published shape authoritative instead of aspirational. The translation layer is a serializer module that builds the wire DTO field by field, so internal properties are never spread into a response, while the boundary itself is convention plus module layout (src/internal/** and the package exports map), since JavaScript has no compiler-enforced visibility. node:http alone replaces nothing here - routing, validation, documentation and versioning would all be hand-written.
pitfalls: Spread-based responses (res.json({ ...entity })) publish every internal field, including ones added later by an unrelated refactor.
Without validation middleware the OpenAPI document is a lie the moment a handler is edited: the document describes the intended contract, the validator is what enforces it.
Unversioned 'temporary' routes become the de-facto contract; the moment a consumer uses one it is published and can no longer be moved.
